shadow:
The plane drops without warning. The seatbelt sign comes on. For a second the floor of the world is gone and the stomach does not know which way is up. That lurch has a frequency, and it runs much wider than air pockets.

Turbulence is the sense that something could break at any moment. It rides under the news, under the love affairs, under the sex and the guilt and the long arguments that loop back to the same place. A life caught in it feels like one episode after another.

Most people read this as bad luck, or as proof the world is hostile. That reading is the trap. The thing being feared is not the suffering itself, it is the fear of the suffering, and the fear is what does the overwhelming. Mind floods, emotions flood, the body floods, and the heart shuts its door to keep the water out.

But the storm has a purpose. It is trying to break something open, not destroy it. The shaking is rough on whatever wants to stay rigid. There is a seed down inside the worst of it, and the seed only cracks under that kind of pressure.
repressive: Some people meet turbulence by holding very still. They keep the surface calm at any cost, terrified of change, and the storm goes inward instead. It coils into the nerves. It does not look like fear. It is.
reactive: Others meet it by making more storm. They spill the turbulence outward as drama and blame, affairs and concealment, and the crisis they would not feel cleanly comes back from somewhere unexpected, looping the same lesson.
gift:
Something changes when a person stops bracing. The storm still comes, the news is still the news, the loss still lands. But the heart does not slam shut this time. It recoils for a breath, then steadies, and the person looks the thing in the eye and lets it all the way in.

This is the gift of humanity, and it is plainer than it sounds. The mind can be overwhelmed. The emotions can. An open heart cannot, because it has no walls to be breached. It just keeps widening to hold whatever arrives.

This is earned, not given. It belongs to people who have been through their own dark stretches and came out still able to feel. They stop reading their pain as punishment and start reading it as something that taught them. That shift makes them safe to be near. When the light darkens in someone else, they are the one who lights up. People in distress walk toward them without being told to.

And the closing is allowed. The heart will shut now and then, briefly, because that is human too. The work is small. Forgive it, coax it back, open again. Then again.
siddhi:
Far enough through the fire, suffering stops being suffering. It does not vanish. It changes into something with no other name, the way a smell rises off the ground after a storm has passed and the air is washed.

This is compassion, and it is not the soft motherly thing people picture. It is the whole truth of a person rushing forward to meet the pain in front of them. The boundary between one heart and all hearts has worn through, so what moves in another moves here too.

A person this far along has sunk so deep into helplessness once that nothing can frighten them now. The fear is simply gone. They tend to walk back toward the places where the light is most darkened, the wards, the wars, the wretched. And the seed that was buried in the turbulence all along, the one the storm was always trying to crack, was this. It was never the enemy. It was compassion, waiting in the dark for the moment a person finally let go.
